identity.description: Minecraft Forge's capability system exposing normalized item, fluid, and energy transfer contracts (IItemHandler, IFluidHandler, IEnergyStorage) that Java mods commonly implement for machine and storage behavior.

constraints: LGPL-2.1: requires attribution and that modifications to Forge itself remain LGPL-2.1

Forge's own LICENSE.txt explicitly states mods referencing Forge via ordinary Java linkage are not bound by Forge's license terms; this entry records only the public capability contract, not Forge source

requiredState: slot count and per-slot stack identity (IItemHandler#getSlots, #getStackInSlot)
tank count and per-tank fluid identity/capacity (IFluidHandler#getTanks, #getTankCapacity)
inputSemantics: insertItem(slot, stack, simulate) returns the remainder that could not be inserted
receiveEnergy(maxReceive, simulate) returns the amount actually accepted
outputSemantics: extractItem(slot, amount, simulate) returns the extracted stack
drain(resource/maxDrain, action) returns the drained fluid stack
extractEnergy(maxExtract, simulate) returns the amount actually extracted

implementationPattern: Capability-typed handler interfaces (IItemHandler/IFluidHandler/IEnergyStorage) queried per-side from a block entity, each supporting a simulate flag on every mutating call so callers can test an operation's outcome before committing it
limitations: isItemValid(slot, stack) filtering is advisory; handlers may still accept invalid items unless the caller checks first
IFluidHandler tank identity does not guarantee same-index stability across ticks in all implementations
bedrockFeasibilityHint: Bedrock has no native equivalent capability system; a faithful adapter must expose the same simulate-before-commit semantics through Hydraulic's own transfer bridge rather than a single non-reversible mutation call

strongIndicators: Forge capability contracts are stable, extensively documented, and used by the overwhelming majority of Forge tech mods
License file explicitly clarifies that referencing these interfaces does not bind mod code to Forge's LGPL-2.1 terms
gaps: This entry documents the public interface contract only; it does not inspect any specific mod's implementation

reviewNotes: Reviewed 2026-09-11 against the public Forge documentation site and the repository's own LICENSE.txt (confirmed LGPL-2.1 with an explicit non-infectivity clause for referencing mods).
No Forge source code was copied into Hydraulic; only the documented public capability contract was recorded.
